chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from one of our companions, from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him), said:
He was asked about the gathering of water in the bathhouse from the bathing of people, which touches the garment. He said: There is no problem.
ai.seo_question: Is the water in a public bathhouse considered pure (tahir) for use in Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that water collected in a bathhouse from people's bathing is not considered impure (*najis*) and remains permissible for use, such as for washing clothes or performing ablution. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the mere presence of humans or their general bodily fluids does not automatically render water impure, distinguishing it from specific impurities like urine or feces. The narration underscores the practical ease (*taysir*) in ritual purity laws, allowing believers to utilize common water sources without excessive caution regarding minor impurities.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abu Yahya Al Wasity, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Maazy<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the gathering of the water in the bathhouse, from the bathing of the people, hitting the clothes’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from abu Yahya al-Wasitiy from certain persons of our people who have said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, the one before, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
was asked about accumulated water in bathhouses used by people which pollutes clothes. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
